input.quote: 13.3 Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.
input.rationale: The grant meets our preferred position. Section 13.1 extends the subscription grant to Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf (plus Authorized Users), and is worldwide and non-exclusive with no "non-transferable" or "revocable" language. Section 13.2 gives Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to paid-up software and Vendor Technology embedded in Deliverables, including contractor support rights, and Section 14.3 confirms that licence covers Vendor Technology needed to use a Deliverable. Section 13.3 permits transfer to an Affiliate or successor (consistent with the consent-free M&A assignment right in Section 24.1) and limits any revocation or suspension to a material uncured payment or use breach after notice and a reasonable cure opportunity, tracking the Section 9.1 cure regime. Section 10.1 preserves paid-up licences after termination. The Section 13.4 restrictions are narrow (no knowing reverse engineering subject to statutory carve-out, no interference or security bypass, no unlawful use) and expressly do not limit authorized security testing or use of Customer Data and output. No redline needed.
